utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Ms. Gopalan, the next witness is ready?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, he is, Your Honours. The next witness is Mr. Hazir Berisha, and his evidence will be relevant to paragraphs 25 to 32 of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Would you please read aloud the affirmation shown to you on the card.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Ms. Gopalan has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Berisha.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Hazir Isuf Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: What is your date of birth, Mr. Berisha?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: December 17th, 1960.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Where were you born, Mr. Berisha?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I was born in Qyshk village.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And where do you live now?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: In the same village.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Berisha, did you give a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal in May 2008?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And have you recently had the opportunity to review the statement recently?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Not before I came here. No. Not before coming here.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review the statement upon coming to the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: In English.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And having reviewed the statement, I understand that you had a number of corrections to make to it, mainly to certain figures and numbers mentioned. I'm going to take you to -- through these corrections.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd like to call up 65 ter 05123, and with Your Honours' leaves, may I provide the witness with a hard copy of his statement in Albanian to assist him with the correction process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, in paragraph 25, page 4, of your statement, you say that there were maybe 50 or 60 men and approximately 240 women and children. Was there a correction you wished to make to the number of men that you mentioned at paragraph 25 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And what was the correction you wished to make?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: From 50 to 60 to 40 to 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 30 you wished to make another correction to the figures stated in that paragraph. At present it reads: "A soldier responded saying that there were 60 or 65." What is the correction you wished to make to that figure?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: The same correction, 40 to 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And in paragraph 57 of your statement, you described the injuries that you suffered. It currently reads that you were injured once on your left knee with an entry and exit wound and once on your right shin, shattering the bone. What is the correction you wished to make to that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Also on the right knee.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That you were also injured on the right knee? Is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And in paragraph 67, you say that you remained in the garden of the house for about an hour. What was the correction you wished to make to that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: The time. It was about four hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally, in paragraph 63, the sentence currently reads: "From the window of this room I was able to see the road that I had walked along to get to the houses." What was the correction you wished to make in that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Not the road that I had come but the road that the forces had come to the place where we were before coming there.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify, so at -- with your corrections it should read: "From the window of this room, I was able to see the road that the forces had walked along." Is that correct? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: The road, yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, having made these corrections to your statement, Mr. Berisha, are you satisfied that it's true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and recollection?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender 65 ter 05123 into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00796, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I will now read out the in-court summary for Mr. Berisha. The witness was born and raised in Qyshk, Kosovo, and is a survivor of the 14 May massacre in the village of Qyshk. He will testify on the -- testify that on the commencement of the NATO bombing he heard that the Serbian police and army were killing and beating Kosovo Albanians in villages surrounding Qyshk, as well as looting the houses. In mid-April 1999, the Serbian police and army entered the Qyshk village and set some houses on fire. They also returned to the village a few days later. On the 14th of May, 1999, the Serbian police and army entered the village of Qyshk again. The witness escaped for fear of being identified as a possible KLA member and went to the centre of the village where about 300 people had congregated. About 70 police and soldiers surrounded them and ordered a separation of men from the women and children. There were approximately 50 men and around 240 women and children. All this time the Serbian forces were firing their weapons. After the villagers were asked to empty their pockets of all valuables, the men were ordered to walk away from the women and children. The women and children were ordered into a courtyard opposite to where the witness was standing. Shortly after, the women and children started screaming as the house that they were standing outside was set on fire. The witness will further testify that of the men, some were initially sent away in one direction, and the remaining group of men were divided into two groups. They were sent in different directions. The witness's group was first directed into Sadik Gashi's house but later moved to Sahit Gashi's house. In the house, Serbian police started shooting at the witness and the group of men he was with. The witness was injured in his legs. The Serb forces then set the house on fire. They returned shortly after, and the witness saw a small canister being thrown into the room. The room was filled with black smoke which made it difficult for the witness to breathe. The witness escaped from the burning house by jumping out of the window and crawled away. The roof of the house collapsed after he escaped. From where he was, the witness could still hear Serb forces giving orders to set things on fire. The witness nursed his injured foot until he got assistance from a woman in the area. He remained in the village until mid-June, until he got medical attention elsewhere. The witness names those he remembered who were with him in the house on the 14th of May. The witness was the sole survivor of the men in this group, and he suffers a permanent limp as a result of the injuries he sustained that day. That's the end of the summary.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask you a few questions about your statement, Mr. Berisha. If I could take you to paragraph 9 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could I call up the statement on e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 9, you speak about hearing stories in the media just after the NATO bombing, about killing and beating and looting against Kosovo Albanian civilians by the Serbian police and army. Mr. Berisha, what was the source of these stories and the media reports that you heard about?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: After the NATO air-strikes began, the Serb forces started to take revenge against the civilian population, and I heard from various media outlets that they have killed, looted, and driven away the Albanian population in sign of revenge for the NATO intervention in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And you also mentioned that these incidents took place in surrounding villages. If you recall, could you name some of these villages, please?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. In Fushe e Pejes nearby, Katundi i Ri, Lebovic, in other villages that I don't remember the names now.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Just to clarify, the name that you mentioned is Fushe e Pejes, Katundi i Ri, and what's the final village, please?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Lebovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to take you to the events in mid-April. This is in paragraph 10 of the witness's statement. You say that around the 16th or 17th of April the Serbian police and army entered the village of Qyshk and that they visited a number of houses and set fire to some of them, including the house of your neighbour, Sadri Lajci. What ethnicity was your neighbour Sadri Lajci, Mr. Berisha?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: He was Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And if you recall, what was the ethnicity of the owners of the other houses that were set on fire?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you remember any of the names of the owners of these other houses?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you. You mentioned earlier in your statement at paragraph 5 that there were three Serb families living in the village of Qyshk. Do you know if on that day their houses were set on fire?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Does that mean you don't know that they were on fire or that they were not set on fire?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: They were not set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You then say that on this day, around seven men entered the yard of your house and that you left your home with your wife, children, and extended family. Mr. Berisha, why did you decide to leave your home then?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: If you want me to explain, I will. That day, after I left my house with my tractor with a trailer; with my family; my extended family, my brothers and their respective families; I saw about seven policemen and soldiers entering the yard of my house. And even though they didn't do anything wrong that day, I saw them when they entered it. We went on with our trip towards the lower part of the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: If they didn't do anything on that day, why did you decide to leave with your family?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: They started to set fire to the houses and to fire in the air. That's why we started to leave the village. In the middle of the village, in the centre of the village, near the cemetery, a little bit below the cemetery, we stopped -- we were stopped by the police and the army, and they told us to go back because we shouldn't leave the village, they said. If you want me, I can recount the whole story here.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: No. That's sufficient for now, Mr. Berisha. Thank you. Now, I would like to ask you some questions about the Serbian men involved in this incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: This is set out in paragraph 14 of the witness statement. If I could call up 65 ter 5258, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, could you describe for us the men who were involved with -- in setting the houses on fire on the 16th and 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. This one in the middle. The second on my left was there that day. The third on my left-hand side was also there, but not very near.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence objects to the photographs being shown since we don't know who took the photographs, when, and we don't know the source of the photographs. Therefore, in our view the photographs cannot be used as evidence in this case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's a somewhat similar objection to one that Mr. Djurdjic has made on more than one occasion. It's not the practice that would always apply in this Tribunal, Mr. Djordjevic. It's a matter of whether the people or the scene in the photograph are sufficiently and reliably identified by the witness which determines whether or not it will be admitted. We'll see whether that condition is satisfied. Thank you. Yes, Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, just to take a step back, do you recognise any of the men that you see in the photograph before you?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: That day I recognised these two I have in front of me and some others. These two in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And had you seen these two men before mid-April when they came to your village?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes -- no. I apologise. No, not before that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you know who these two men in the middle are?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Later I found out that they are Srecko Popovic and Kastratovic, Nenad Kastratovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And how did you find this out, Mr. Berisha?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: From the photos. I understood that they were the same persons that were -- that were there that night -- that day, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And what did these two men do on the 16th or 17th of May when they came to your village?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: On the 16th or 17th of May, after we left with our tractors and went to the centre of the village with the families, they ordered us to go back, because they said we were not supposed to leave the village. That day, they confiscated one -- two weapons from Ibrahim Vokshi and told us to go back to our houses and leave the houses only when they told us to.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, when you speak about the confiscation of the weapons - that's in paragraph 11 of your statement - you refer to a senior officer. Is the senior officer you mentioned on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. This one in the middle. The second on my left. Srecko Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And was anyone else in this photograph involved in this confiscation of weapons that you talk about?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Srecko Popovic, but I think he was staying a little bit further away compared to the rest of the group. I don't know if I made myself clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: If you could just clarify who else was involved in the confiscation of the weapons. You mentioned Srecko Popovic initially, and I asked you if there was anyone else involved.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but he is not here among the ones that I see in front of me in this picture.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: If we could go to the second page of this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise the man on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. It's the same person that I saw in the previous photo, Srecko Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And could we please go to page 3 of this exhibit. Is it possible to enlarge it? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, do you recognise any of the men on this photograph? Perhaps we could start with the bottom left-hand corner, the man with the headband, and work our way across.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: The one with the headband was a former policeman in Peja municipality at the time. The one in the middle wearing a hat was called Salipur, and the one with the uniform to my right with a machine-gun is called Nevzat. I've mentioned before that these were the two that communicated between each other. They were like officers in charge. They communicated with the persons from the period -- previous picture. The one seated to my right with a sort of a red thing hanging over him was also with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. We will come back to these photographs in a moment just to clarify the various individuals that you have mentioned, but for now I would like to take you to the events of the 14th of May, 1999. And you talk about this in paragraph 19 of your statement. You say: "At approximately 7.15 hours on 14 May I was at home with my extended family and a number of co-villagers." Could you tell us what happened next?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. It is a little bit difficult for me, but I will do my best to tell you everything that happened. On the 14th of May, at around 7.00 or 7.15, we were drinking coffee in the yard of the house with other villagers. This is a common thing in our village. We heard gunshots being fired in the upper part of the village. I went out and saw police and army coming towards the village, towards the houses in the village. I returned in the yard. I told my family about this, and my next door neighbour. I said to them that the police and army entered the village and are firing. I saw them in great numbers. I don't know the exact number, but they were a large group coming towards the village. Having informed my next door neighbour, I went back home. My mother begged me to leave the house and not remain there with them because she feared I might get killed since I was able-bodied man and in their eyes a possible member of the KLA. That's why I decided to leave the house. I walked about 200 metres towards a neighbourhood in the middle of the village. That's where I stopped and observed the terrain. I saw that everything was being set on fire, that they were firing in the air. Later on, I went further down the village towards the centre where the incident happened. There I met other villagers from the Lushi and Kelmendi families. A little bit later, about seven to ten minutes later, they came from all sides and ordered us to come out to the road passing by the graveyard.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Berisha. I'll just stop you there to clarify one or two points that you've made. You say: "A little bit later, about seven to ten minutes later, they came from all sides and ordered us to come out to the road passing by the graveyard." Who are you referring to when you say "they came from all sides"?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: The police and the army. Whenever I say "they," I would kindly ask you to know that I'm referring to the police and the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You mention the Lushi and Kelmendi families, that they also were gathered in the centre of the village. Now, what about the women and children in the group? Where were they?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Children, women, everybody was gathered there. My family was not there. However, the other families were there with women and children. If I'm not mistaken, we were about 250 people there. So there were children, women, men, all together there. If you want me, I can continue now by telling you how things -- how the incident happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes. If you could please continue, Mr. Berisha.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: When they came and threatened us and ordered us to go to the main road and for the men to go on one side of the road and the women and children on the other side of the road, we were then told to throw on the ground everything we had in our pockets, money, cigarettes, whatever happened to be in our pockets at the time. They gave the same order to the women who were on the other side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, just to stop you there. If you remember, was there anyone in particular in the group who ordered you to throw everything that you had in your pockets on the ground?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. Precisely this person here with the police uniform, with the Kalashnikov or machine-gun in his hands. It was him and another person whom I don't really recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Just to stop you there, are you referring to the photograph that's on the screen before you when you say, "Precisely this person with the police uniform and Kalashnikov"?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, that person.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you know who he is, Mr. Berisha?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I later learned that his name was Nebojsa Minic.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could continue, please. You stopped when the order was given for the women to also empty their pockets. What happened next?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Next they took two children of the age of 13 or 14, perhaps, and ordered them to collect everything that was thrown on the ground, documents, ID cards, money, everything that we this thrown on the ground. They designated one of the children to collect the money and the other one to the collect the documents, ID cards, and other items. Once this task was completed, one of them went to the women, and I remember how he grabbed one child by the hair and said to the women, "If you don't empty your pockets and throw on the ground everything you have, I will cut the throat of this child." Out of fear, the women threw on the ground everything they had on them, gold and jewellery, everything they had on them. Shortly after, the person that I mentioned several times asked one of the other guys as to what was the number of men there. I remember that the other man said more than 40, and then he replied to his colleague by saying, "Dobro," which is good. His wishes were satisfied --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Berisha.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: -- and throughout this time they were firing in our presence.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to clarify, you have referred to a person you have mentioned several times. Do you remember what his name is?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Srecko Popovic. As I said, I learned his name later. And Nebojsa Minic.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: But just to be clear, the individual that you referred to as the person who said, "Dobro," and this is the senior man that you talk about in paragraph 30 of your statement. Am I correct that his name is Srecko Popovic? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And you also mention that ID cards were collected. Do you know what happened to these ID cards?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't know what happened to the ID cards, whether they were burned or taken away. I really don't know. They were firing in our presence near our feet and in the air, and then they ordered us to take a small path which was about 20 or 30 metres away from where we were to a house of Ajet Gashi. The men started to enter Ajet Gashi's house. Twelve or 13 entered the house, and the rest were told to stand with their heads -- backs on the wall because there was not enough room. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Just a moment. You have been telling us about what happened to the men. What about the women and children? Where were they at this stage?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Then I'll try to recall things chronologically. The women and children were taken to a house across the place where I was. This house was on fire. Part of women and children were taken to this house and another part to the next house's yard. The women and children were taken to the yard of the house that was opposite me. The house was on fire, and they were screaming because they were scared. This I could see, because the gate to the yard was open.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, did you see who set the house on fire?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: The police and the army. They were the ones that burned down everything they saw there. Not the persons, but these people were inside there.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you please clarify your answer? I asked who did you see -- my apologies, did you see who set the house on fire, and you said the police and the army. What --

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: They were the ones that were setting the houses on fire. I didn't see this personally, but once they entered the yard and when they came out, the house started to burn. But I think -- I can go into more details, but I think I am clear enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. You are clear enough on that point. Thank you. I now would like to take you to paragraph 43 of your statement, and here you say: "A senior soldier directed some of the Serbian forces to take the men from the compound behind me, saying take them their." And you then state that the senior soldier made a certain hand gesture. Could you show us, please, what this gesture was that the senior soldier made? If you could just show us.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. He was crossing his hands like this, and I understood this to mean take them there and finish them. And later on, I learned that this actually was true. This is exactly what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me just stop you there, Mr. Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Let the record indicate that the witness made a gesture of crossing his hands over each other with the right hand moving horizontally from the left to the right and the left hand moving from the right to the left.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, you say -- you explain what the hand gesture meant to you, and you say this is exactly what happened. Can you explain what it is that happened to these men, please?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: The men that were in the yard that I mentioned earlier, 12 or 13 of them, were taken out of the house towards the graveyard. I could still see them from there. I later learned this. They went towards the house of Syl Gashi. Later on, I heard the gunshots fired from automatic rifles; and shortly after, I saw flames coming out of the house. I would say ten minutes later, after smoke and fire was coming out of the house, those that had led the group of men towards that house, these soldiers and policemen, came back and told Srecko Popovic and Nebojsa Minic - although there were many, many others whom I didn't know - they told them that they finished them off by making the same gesture with their hands that I already showed you. Shall I continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Immediately afterwards, they discussed something between themselves. They took our watches from our wrists. The more valuable watches were taken, put aside, whereas those cheaper ones to another side. Later on, Srecko Popovic divided into two the group we were in, directed one part of the group in one direction and the other into another direction. The group I was in, we all had our hands behind our backs and walked towards the graveyard, whereas the other group walked in the opposite direction. When we came near Sadik Gashi's house, we were escorted by five policemen and soldiers. There in the vicinity of this house one of them said, "Not here, because there might be stench." We proceeded towards Sahit Gashi's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Can I just stop you there, Mr. Berisha? When one of the soldiers said, "Not here because there might be stench," what did you understand that to mean?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I thought they were going to burn us alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And did they say anything else to your group as they were taking you to the house of Sadik Gashi initially and then later to Sahit's house?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: We proceeded towards Sadik's house. Along the way, they were firing all the time. They were cursing us, saying to us, "Where is NATO now? Where is Tony Blair?" and many, many other offensive words they used. We went to the corridor of the house. One of these five policemen and soldiers opened the door of the corridor, entered, and then we from the group entered with our hands still on the back of our heads. He open the door to a room and order us to go into that room where the execution occurred later on. It was a four by four room. It had two sofas in an L shape. They ordered us to sit on this L-shaped Sofa. I sat on the corner. On my left I had Arian Lushi, whereas on my right I had Jusuf Shala, who were -- happened to be guests in our village from another village. These soldiers and policemen stopped at the entry, four of them as far as I recall, and I remember very well when I saw the fire fired from the machine-gun. The first bullets were fired into my direction. It was uninterrupted fire directed towards my side by one of them and another one directed his fire on the other side of the Sofa. I was not wounded then. The fire stopped for a short time, then a burst of fire came from the opposite direction, from the left side, and I was hit the first time on my left leg and the second time on my right knee. After this second round of -- volley of fire, there was a brief pause. You could hear the cries of the men who had been shot. There was still people alive amongst them. And then I heard them fire one bullet on each of the men. They started from my left side and continued up to one or two persons away from me and there they stopped. I don't know the reason why they stop. Maybe they ran out of bullets. I survived this execution. It stopped. They went outside. I tried to open my eyes a little bit and have a look around in the room where I was. And on my left I saw them piled on top of each other, and I saw blankets on the upper part of the room to my left. I touched Arian Lushi. He was dead. I tried to move him. He wasn't moving. Isuf Shala who was to my right was also dead. I was thinking of getting up. They were covered with sponge. I was thinking of getting up when I saw them piled like that, but in split of a second I decided to look through the window. The window was behind me, and instinctively I turned my head and saw five of them talking among each other. One of them broke away from that group and walked into the corridor of the house. He had kind of a bottle or something in his canister, a longish shaped, and threw it in. I started to catch fire very fast. The fire caught my face, and at that time I was -- I didn't know where I was, whether on the ground or floating. For a moment I couldn't see anything. I thought I was buried deep in the ground. I was trying to stand on my foot. I couldn't, but I guess God helped me. I came next to the door. To tell you the truth, I tried to stand up not to survive that execution but to be killed by a bullet and not be burnt alive. After I went to the door, I started to breathe and to see. There I saw that they were no longer there and decided to walk in the direction of the next room using my left leg. There I saw that the room was covered in flames. Even if there were fire -- a fire brigade there, they wouldn't have been able to extinguish it. I went to the window, and I saw parked outside in the street, tractors, trucks, cars. I didn't see any policemen or soldiers at that moment. I opened the window, and holding in my hands the right leg because it was injured, broken, I used the left leg and crawled out of the window. It was about 1 metre and 70 centimetres high. And then I crawled on my back until the corner of the house. It may be 5 or 6 metres away, I'm not clear. And then I went to the corner to the fence surrounding -- dividing the houses. It was -- there was wire there in that -- in that fence. And nobody was there to help me. During all this time, I tried to help myself. But I could hear the moans and the anguished cries, the sounds of cars, tractors. During all this time there was continuous -- continuous fire and shots. I feel very excited at this moment because I'm reliving, you know, what I went through that day. As I said, I tried to help myself. I tied up my right leg with my belt, and I looked at my left leg. I tried to tie the wound in order to prevent the blood from coming out.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha --

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Half an hour later --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Let me just stop you there. Thank you very much. If we could just go back to the house you were in. You say that you jumped out of the window and that the house was on fire. Do you know what caused the house to burn?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: As I said, there were some blankets there which were on fire. And as I said, they threw this bottle with gas, I think, and that helped the fire. And so as I said, I couldn't breathe at that moment. I lost consciousness. After -- even ten days after that, I used to spit out blood. I don't know if I'm clear. If you have questions, you may ask me.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: The blanket that you say were on fire, did you see how they caught fire?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I only saw them after these people left. I saw the blankets that were burning. How can I explain to you? They were set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: How many of you were in this group of yours?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: To my recollection, 12 or 13. Even though I don't like to mention names, but I think about 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And of those 12 or 13 men, how many survived this incident?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Only myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: In paragraph 64 of your statement you speak about the roof of this house you were in collapsing. Do you know why this roof collapsed?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: From the fire, because the entire house was set on fire, and then the roof collapsed in, caved in, and it fell down.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And you also say that when you were in the yard after you jumped out of the window, you heard activity around you, and you heard orders being given to set things on fire. Do you remember what language these orders were given in?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: In Serbian. In Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, following this incident, Mr. Berisha, what injuries did you sustain?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I was injured on both my legs, on my left, on the knee of the left leg, and on the right knee, and on the hip of the left leg. They were simultaneous injuries I sustained, and my right leg was broken in seven or eight places. Only the skin held the pieces together. Do you want further explanations how that happened?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: No, that's sufficient. Thank you. But how -- let me rephrase the question. You have mentioned a number of injuries. Do you suffer any permanent injuries following this indent?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. My right leg is about 4 or 5 centimetres shorter. Because of that, I limp even today.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I use crutches.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, earlier in your testimony you mentioned that there were two other groups of men that were taken away. One went to the house of Syl Gashi you mentioned. Now, you were in the remaining two groups. What about the third group? Where did they go? Whose house were they taken to?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: The group I was in was divided in two parts. I don't know where they were taken to, but at a later phase I realised that they were taken to the house of Deme Gashi.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And what happened to the men who were taken to the house of Deme Gashi?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: They suffered the same fate. They were all killed. Only one survived. Iljaz Kelmendi in the house of Syl Gashi, Isa Gashi survived. So God willed that in each of the three houses one survived.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you recall, how many men were killed in your village Qyshk on that day, the 14th of May?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: A total of 41 from the entire village, including men from the upper part of the village and the part we were in. So a total of 41.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Berisha, do you know if there were any other killings in villages chose to Qyshk on that day, if you know?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. On the same day after Qyshk village they went to Pavlan village, Zahaq village. In these three villages, Qyshk, Pavlan, and Zahaq, maybe a total of 80 persons were killed in half a day.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And in your own village of Qyshk, were there any killings prior to the 14th of May, if you know?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, there were. I don't remember the exact date, but it was either on the 13th or the 14th when I heard shots. And there was a man and a woman taken from the city and killed in the vicinity of the road, Peja-Prishtina road, near a store there. They were elderly people who we were not able to bury because, as I said, we suffered our own fate. And I think they -- their corpse -- their bodies were eaten by the dogs.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you know who was responsible for the killing of these elderly folk either on the 13th or 14th of May?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: The police and soldiers were those who took them.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: How do you know that, Mr. Berisha?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Because they were the ones who did such things. Everything that happened was committed by the police and the soldiers. And you can -- you could see their presence from a distance. They were the only ones that were doing these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Did you see police or soldiers in the village of Qyshk round about the time this elderly couple was killed?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Not in the village, inside the village. This happened in the vicinity of the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So did you see any police or soldiers in the vicinity of the road?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. When the murder took place, I heard the shots, and I saw a car with police and soldiers passing by. That car passed. After, we heard the shots. So we saw the police car passing by. After, we heard the shots, but we couldn't take their bodies. This happened at about 7.00, 8.00 in the evening. On the next day, they came to our village. So later we heard that their bodies were eaten by dogs. This was just to give you an explanation about what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And you also mentioned some killings in the village of Pavlan and Zahac. Do you know who was responsible for those killings in the nearby villages?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: The same people, because the same persons who were in our village continued their work further away in the Pavlan and Zahaq village, because during the day we heard constant shots and could see the smoke or fire coming from all over the place. I didn't mention before, but besides the shots you could see the smoke coming from all over the place.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to clarify the names of some of the individuals in the photograph before you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I think we still have it on our screen, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned during your testimony today an individual named Nebojsa Minic. Is he on the photograph before you? Could you describe --

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: -- or identify him in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: He's the person with the police uniform. He has a machine-gun in his hand, and he was the person, as I said earlier, I'm repeating, the person, the key person, with Srecko Popovic. These are the two key persons regarding what happened that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to clarify, is this the person who's standing with the cigarette in his mouth?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And on the 14th of May, did you see anyone else in this photograph in your village?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I saw this one with a band, headband, but also the other one who is sitting on my right-hand side. I think he has something red on his shoulder. Now I remember they were there too.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: The man with the headband, had you seen him prior to the incident in your village on the 14th of May?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. He was a policeman even before, and this one in the middle was also -- this one with the cap was also a policeman. Both of them were policemen even before what happened in the village. Even before the war, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, you --

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Before 1998, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned the man with the cap standing right in the middle. Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, I know his pseudonym, Salipur. I don't know his real name.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That's sufficient. Thank you. What else did you know about Salipur apart from the fact that he was a policeman?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Every citizen that was stopped in the street, he was maltreated by this person. He was notorious for the maltreatment of people. The maltreatment of Albanians, not other ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: If we could move on to the next page of this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. It's me there in the house where the crime was committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And when you say in the house the crime was committed, you mean the house of -- whose house are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: The house of Sahit Gashi.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And do you know when this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: No. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And do you know who took this photograph, if you do?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, just to move on to another topic, you say in your statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Gopalan, we've come and gone with these photographs more than once. Are you proposing to tender them?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I was hoping to show them once more, another page, before I tendered it all at once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: But I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, no. You do it your way, as long as you haven't forgotten. But before you finish with the witness, you may learn from him, if you could, how he knew the names of the people that he is naming in his evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, during your testimony today you have mentioned a number of names. Popovic, for example, Minic. Could you explain to us how it is you came to know the names of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I think I am -- if I'm not mistaken, that I didn't know them by names, but from the photos I recognise them by sight. But later on I learned that they were called as I mentioned, Salipur, this nickname -- this person I knew personally as a policeman, even though I never had anything to do with him, but I knew that everybody called him by this nickname. The other policeman that I mentioned later, I didn't know his name, but people called him Pucrrani because his face was full of pimples. Pucrrani in Albanian means pimple face. Then, later, as I said, I learned their names.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I hope I'm clear now.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could just go back to the photograph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Not for my purposes. From who was this learned?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I will ask the question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Who was it who told you the names of these people? How did you learn this?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: After we identified them on these photos, later on I could identify them through a book which I have at home. But I don't know the person who identified them by name, because there were many people who identified them. I can't give you any name. But I have a book; in that book you have all these names. If you want some more explanation, you can ask me.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, these -- this book that you say that has the photos, when did you see this book for the first time?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: This book was given to me as a present by those who collected these notes. Because I was a participant in the event. Because of that, they gave that book to me as a present.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And do you know who it is that gave you this book? Those who collected the notes, who are they?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Radio Vojs [phoen] if I'm not mistaken. I have given several statements that there may be other persons who have collected such notes. Radio Vojs as far as I know is one of them. I don't know the accurate name of the organisation or the persons who collected such notes. At this moment, it doesn't come to my mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if that sufficiently clear, or would you like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is clear, but it leaves us without any reliable basis for names, as you would realise. The witness has been told or has been given a book with names in it. That doesn't help us reach the point of identification of the individuals.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: If I could just go back to the previous page of this -- of this exhibit before us. Now, you mentioned today someone called Pucrrani. Is that person in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, the one with the band, headband. On my left side.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And where had you seen him before?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: He was a policeman in the town of Peja.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this photograph that you have before you, when did you see it for the first time?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I saw this photo with the other photos. I don't think I have mentioned it in my statement, but after our killing, let's say, there were some investigators and different organisations that came to ask us about that incident, and they showed us some photos. They showed us these photos, and we identified the persons we knew. This person that I'm mentioning, this one you asked me about, I've seen him several times in Peja, because he was a policeman there. The other person wearing a cap, he was also a policeman in the town of Peja. Later on, based on the photos, I don't know who asked me because I've seen many, but during one of these occasions they gave me this book I mentioned; but I don't recall who was the first to show me the photos and where this happened. Very frankly, I am saying that I have seen such photos several times, but I don't remember when and who showed them to me. If I'm not clear, I'm sorry. You may ask me again.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just have another short topic to deal with. With your leave, I wonder if we to take our break at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We must take our first break and resume at 10 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, just to pick up where we left off. We were talking about the photograph on the screen before you, and you say that they showed us this photographs and we identified the persons we knew. Could you tell us, Mr. Berisha, when you say, "We identified the persons we knew," did you identify them by name or by sight?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: By sight at the time. As far as the one with the headband is concerned, I know that he was a policeman, although I didn't mention his name in the statement. I knew that he was a policeman, as was the person with the cap.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, this person with the headband, how did you know that he was a policeman?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I think I mentioned it earlier. He was a policeman in Peja. He was an active policeman, as they called them. Although he is wearing a military uniform here, at the time he had a police uniform. They used to wear the uniforms they wanted regardless of whether it was military or police uniform. That's why I'm saying he was a policeman, although he is wearing a military uniform on this picture. If you want me to give you more details, I can do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you say, At that time he had a police uniform, what time are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I'm talking about the incident of the 14th and about the time when the war was ongoing. The person with the headband and the one with the cap were policemen even before 1998. I'm stating this with full responsibility. Although they're wearing military uniforms in this picture, they were policemen and wore police uniforms at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now, the other men who participated in the incident on the 14th of May in Qyshk, were they also wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And could you describe for us what uniforms they were wearing, please.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: On the 14th of May, as well as on the 16th and 17th, the police members were wearing blue police uniform with grey mixture of colours, camouflage, as they call it, whereas the army were wearing green camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: When you refer to the 16th and 17th, could you please clarify what month you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: April, about one month before the massacre in the village was committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally, if you have a look at the photograph, could you tell us who came to your village, if at all, on the 14th of May? Are they present in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's been made very clear, Ms. Gopalan. You have no need to ask that again.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honours. I seek to tender this exhibit into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, there have been several photographs shown of which this photograph is one. This happens to be Exhibit P772, if I'm correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So it doesn't need to be tendered again. It's identified in the transcript. But you've also shown a photograph of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In a house. A photograph of one of the people in this group photograph standing alone. Are they photographs you intend to tender?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. They're all part of the same 65 ter number. The reason I've included this photograph on the screen separately is because I believe it's slightly clearer than the photograph already in evidence, but with Your Honour's guidance, I'm very happy to just tender the ones -- the remaining ones that I've shown to the witness, which I believe are pages 1 and 2 of this exhibit and the photograph with the witness in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Pages 1 and 2 will be received, photographs 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And they would be assigned P00797, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And also page 4 of this exhibit, please, which is the photograph of the witness himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Pages 1, 2, and 4, Your Honours, will be assign the same exhibit number as P00797.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, at paragraph 23 you say that of the group that was gathered in the village centre and that was surrounded by 70 policemen, this group did not include any members of your family. Where were your family members? This is going back to the 14th of May.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: They were at home. My entire family was in my house. But later on, my mother told me that when the police and army came there my son, who was 11 months at the time, a police or a soldier approached him, put the barrel of his automatic in his mouth, and demanded money from those present or else he threatened to kill the child. My wife was scared to death and could no longer hold my son in her arms. She dropped him. My now late mother gave them 500 Deutschmarks. Later on, they told my family to take the main road towards Peja. Perhaps because of my emotions, I'm overwhelmed with emotion, and I didn't mention everything that happened, but I'm taking this opportunity to tell you now that they were told to go towards Peja, and then they were again sent back home. So they had to come back to the village on two occasions. You may ask me further questions if you want me to clarify any issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: How did they go to Peja on that day?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: That day, the women, children, and elderly who happened to be in their homes were taken by tractors covered with plastic covers in the direction of the town. Not only my family but the other families who had remained in the village at the time were taken towards the town in tractors.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Can you recall how big was this group that was taken towards the town in tractors?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Probably between 200 and 250 people, men, elderly men, children, and women. Maybe even more, but I don't really recall the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And how did you learn about this incident?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I learned about it from my mother, who has died.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And when you say that your family was sent to Peja and returned back, was that on the same day?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Berisha, I'd just like to clarify a question that I asked you. Perhaps the error was in my question. I'd asked you about the incident that took place in mid-April. Perhaps I could read the question for you just to clarify. This is in relation to your answer on the confiscation of weapons from Ibrahim Vokshi and that you were told to go to your house and "leave the house only when they told us to." Now, this incident when you were asked to go back to your house and then return only when they ordered you to do so, when did that take place? Was that on the 16th or 17th of May? That's what's reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: On the 16th or 17th of May, when we were sent back, when we were not allowed to leave the village. This happened on the same day, on the 16th or the 17th. On this same day, Ibrahim Lushi, or Ibrahim Vokshi handed over a hunting rifle and a pistol, a handgun.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: So am I correct that this took place in May and not in April as you say in your statement?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I apologise. I apologise. One month approximately before the May incident, 16th or 17th of April. I'm talking about April now. I apologise for this mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And we also referred to three Serb families living in the village of Qyshk. This is at paragraph 5 of your statement. Could you clarify if this was the total number of Serb families living in Qyshk?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, I mentioned in my statement that there were three households, not three families in the village, because one household can comprise of four or five families. I didn't mention the other houses, because I wasn't sure whether they belonged to Qyshk village or to the village adjacent to Qyshk.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Berisha. I have no further questions for you at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djordjevic, do you cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. If I have -- if I may have a moment to prepare myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. I will be putting questions to you arising from the examination that my learned friend has just completed, and I kindly ask you to give me short answers. Mr. Berisha, can you tell me what is your profession and what was it that you did in late May of 1999? Were you employed? Did you have any sort of occupation at all?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: If you can repeat your question, please. I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: What is your profession? What is your educational background?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I've completed secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: For which particular vocation?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Shoemaker.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I haven't received interpretation. Right. Tell me, were you employed in 1999? Were you working?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I was an employee in the shoe factory, but in 1999 I wasn't working. Nobody was working from the Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: When did you stop working, if you can tell me.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure about the date, but I think it was in 1998. I don't know the exact month.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, was the factory located in Pec, the factory you worked for?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, in Peja.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you employed today?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you have the first contact with the ICTY OTP and their investigators, in which year?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Are you referring to the time when I came here or to a time earlier?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: No. No. My question was when it was that you had the very first contact with the ICTY investigators. You don't need to tell me the month. The year would be enough.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: In May 2008 when I gave my statement, that's when I met them. I met them immediately after the incident occurred, but I don't know the exact date when this meeting took place. I think I'm clear I don't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that your first encounter with the ICTY investigators was back in 1999 and not in 2008, as you've just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: After 1999, many people came to see me, but the statement I gave and why I'm here today, this statement was taken in May last year, 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did you offer to give a statement or did they approach you first?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I gave the statement out of my free will. They came because they were intrigued with this case and the circumstances under which I survived.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I'm interested in. How did you come to inform them that you were the only survivor of the Cuska incident? Was it you, or was it somebody else who informed them of it, or is it the case that you don't know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know how they learnt about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to know if you had filled out a questionnaire on the 28th of July, 1999, which had to do precisely with the events you testified to today. Did you answer questions put to you by an individual who introduced himself or herself as a representative of the committee for human rights and freedoms in Kosovo? Do you recall that? That was the union or alliance for the defence of human rights and freedoms.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: As I already said, I gave many, many statements. I don't remember who came to see me, but I did give many statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What did you have in mind when you said that you gave a statement for the ICTY shortly after the events in Cuska, i.e., in 1999? Who did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Can you -- you're asking me the same question for the second time. I don't remember who came to see me first or second. I gave many, many statements. I think I already answered your question the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not clear on that, and probably nobody else in the courtroom is. My first question to you was -- was about your first contact with the representatives of the ICTY Prosecution. You first said that it was in 2008, and that was the statement you gave which is beyond doubt. However, you also stated that you gave a statement for the Tribunal shortly after the events transpired. Can you please tell me is my understanding correct or not?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: No. At that time, immediately after the incident, I didn't know who was who when they came to see me, and when I gave statements. This statement that we have today is a statement that I gave in 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement you say that you served the military service in 1981 in Nis apparently. What was your occupational speciality, the VES as it was known in the army?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Infantry for the first six months, although in the military booklet, as profession I had "shoemaker" listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you serve the entire military service for the entire term?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Twelve months.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Can you distinguish between the uniforms worn by the Army of Yugoslavia and the uniforms worn by the police in view of the fact that you did the military service?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. They've changed. At that time they were different from what they are now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: In 1981 the uniforms were different from when? Today or 1999? 1999 was ten years ago?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: They were different in 81 from those that we are talking about in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did you know what the military uniforms were like in 1999 and 1998? Was there a barracks close to your village?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: No, there was no barracks close to our village, but I described the uniforms earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Can you do the same thing now since we were mentioning 1999 as compared to 1981?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I was in the army. There was a solid colour uniform. It was a green uniform, a solid green.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the military uniforms looked like in 1999? Were there solid-colour uniforms or were there other sorts of uniform as well?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: If you are asking me about the army, they were camouflage colours. If you ask me about the uniforms in 1999, there were both blue and camouflage blue. The army had green, solid green and the camouflage green uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned blue uniforms. What sort were they? Camouflage or solid blue? What was it that you had in mind when mentioning the colour blue in reference to the army?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I said blue for the police. Don't mix them up. I said the police wore blue, solid blue and camouflage blue uniforms. The army wore green uniforms and camouflage green. I think I'm clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Now it's come up quite clear. Thank you. I suppose you still have your statement dating from May of 2008 that you gave to the OTP. It is in evidence in this case. And I'll ask you to look at paragraph 15, please, which states as follows: "Three or four days after the incident, I was in the centre of the village speaking with a group of maybe eight male friends ..." I have to slow down. I guess it's for the sake of interpretation. " ... including Syl Gashi (now deceased). As we spoke, two vehicles, one army and one police, entered the village and stopped a short distance from where we were standing." In the next paragraph you say that four soldiers came out of the military vehicle and four policemen out of the police vehicle. Can we please set a date on this, since in one of your statements you referred to a certain period of time and described the very same event. Am I right if I say that this event, in fact, refers to the 17th of April, 1999, or am I wrong? Was it earlier or was it later? You have paragraphs 15 and 16 in front of you, so please look at them.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: This happened after the 15th or 16th of April. I cannot be accurate. It might be up to -- up to one, two, or three days, within that time-frame, after the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. That's clear now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask the registrar to call up Exhibit D003-6348. I think that's the English version of the questionnaire, which is an original prepared by the Union for the Defence of Human Rights and Freedoms from Pristina, Kosovo. If I cited it correctly. Let me just check the number. 6348. No, not 63 -- 0348. That's the right number, 0348. D003-0348.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Of course, let's look at page 2. In your statement you say that: "A month before the crime happened, i.e., on the 3rd or 4th of April, 1999, 12 to 13 uniformed persons came in a military jeep and started shooting in the air. They told us that they were regular army and that they wouldn't provoke us. They came on the 17th of April and set the houses on fire and we moved to another neighbourhood where it was safer. They wanted us to hand them over weapons and they appointed the following day as the day to deliver the same. They were regular army, but there were also paramilitaries. They took a nice car, some 10 to 15.000 German marks from Syl Gashi --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. You're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, since Mr. Djordjevic is quoting quite extensively from the statement, I wonder if it's possible to have up an Albanian version of it to assist the witness at the moment. I don't think that's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't know the answer at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be of assistance. It does not exist. I haven't seen an Albanian translation of this statement, and that's why I'm quoting from the statement to save time for the Prosecution, the Court, and myself. I meant to suggest to -- and I suggested that the English version be placed on the screens for all those who use English. I also wanted to call up the Albanian version, but I was unable to find it. That's the only reason why I'm reading out for the benefit of the witness. With your leave, I would proceed to put questions to the witness in relation to his 2008 statement and his 1999 statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would probably be helpful if you could identify what is different about the two and ask if the witness can explain any difference. You've quoted a long section of it, but I think you need to take the witness's mind to what it is that's different as you see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely what I was about to do, Your Honour. I do admit that the quotation was longish, but I wanted to make sure that I cannot be told that I took a part of the witness's statement out of the context in an attempt to facilitate the Defence case in this improper way. However, what I was about to ask the witness before my learned friend stood up was: Why is it now, in 2009, nine years later, he stated that there were -- or rather, In 1999 you stated that there were two vehicles arriving, a police and a military car, whereas in his -- so in 2008 he mentioned police and military car, whereas in 1999 statement he only mentions the regular army without referring to the police. So apparently on the 17th of April, in addition to the jeep, a police car showed up. So where did the police come out of when the witness clearly stated in his statement on the 28th of July, 1999: "They wanted us to hand over our weapons and they set the following day as the deadline. There were regular military personnel, as well as the paramilitaries there." Apparently the witness is familiar with the police because he saw them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, do you have a question for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is: Where does this discrepancy between the two statements come from? Why is he mentioning police forces now in -- or, rather, in 2008, whereas back then in 1999 when his memories of the events were fresh he did not mention the police.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have read it very well from what I see it. I have stated several times it was not the same event. That happened at the beginning of April or the end of March, which means I gave it on the 2nd, on the 3rd of April, and I talked about the regular army. They came by a police jeep and fired in the air, and I saw it with my own eyes. They came there. They fired in the air and said, "Don't be afraid of us. We are regular army," and I'm quoting. "And we won't do anything to you unless you do anything to us." And this happened on the 3rd or 4th. I'm not accurate about the time. It was the beginning of April. Whereas on the 16th of April, I talked about the police and the army, and one or two days after that date they came there with two cars. And I mentioned this in my statement, because this is something I saw it with my own eyes, not -- I didn't hear from others. That they came there after the 16th or the 17th to ask for money, as I said earlier. They said -- they addressed the deceased Syl Gashi, saying that "We didn't find any weapons." They went together to his house. I think they got a BMW car from him, and then they said, up to 3.000 Deutschmark. They took it from Syl Gashi. They took the car and went in the direction of the main road, the Peja road. This is simply by way of explanation in reference to my statement of 1998, 1999. I am speaking about events which I was an eyewitness of and not heard from others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What Mr. Djordjevic pointed out to you is that in the statement you gave in 1999, you said there in respect of the 17th of April, you appear to have said "They were regular army, but there were also paramilitaries." There's no mention of the police, and so he asks you why is it that you now say there were police and army. Can you help us with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try. I said army and police, but someone may describe the army as paramilitaries. I don't know, because I don't know what the people who have gotten down my statement have written there. I have used the word "army."
