People may describe it as paramilitaries, but for me there were police and army, if I am clear now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that help you, Mr. Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope that it helps all of us. At any rate, that's the answer the witness gave us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I have to go back to the 28th of July, 1999, statement where, having read the entire statement carefully, I must say that you did not mention the police once. You solely mentioned the army and paramilitaries. My search engine on the computer said that in the 2008 statement you mention the police on 29 occasions and not once in your 1999 statement. So how come nine years later you mention the police 29 times and you did not mention them once back in 1999 when you testified to the events that had transpired shortly before and when your memories were fresh?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I already gave the answer. I have no other answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: You haven't answered my question though. How come that you did not mention the police in 1991 a single time? You kept referring to regulars, and on a couple of occasions you mentioned some irregulars, but that was it.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't remember to have mentioned the irregular -- irregulars in my statement. Since you are saying this, I'm repeating. There were police and army. I don't know, but I'm saying now that this is what they were, and I'm saying this in full responsibility, irrespective of what you are putting to me in respect of my statement. I am saying this not because I want to accuse anyone by saying that but because this is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I will put to you another part of your statement of the 28th of July, 1999, which does not tally with what you said in 2008. You say the following on page 2, I think paragraph 3: "I went a short distance away so as not to be killed in front of my family. The rest of the family and some 40 guests which had taken refuge in my house remained inside." That's what you said in 1999, whereas nine years later, you say that in your house there were 17 members. It is paragraph 7 of your statement. You say: "In May 1999 I was in Qyshk with my wife and family."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would Mr. Djordjevic please slow down when quoting. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 2008 I was asked only about my narrow family, and I wasn't asked about the overall number of guests in my family. That's why I stated my narrow, close family. My brothers -- the extended family, including my brothers, their wives and son, consisted of 17 members. The truth is that there were 40 others, women, children, men who were there, but I wasn't asked at that time this question that you're putting to me now in 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1999, you -- or, rather, the person who questioned you called those people guests, but it is clear to all of us in the courtroom that one cannot have 40 guests in the house. Who were these people? If I understood well, these 40 people were there on top of the 17 members of your family. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: If you insist on me saying what you want, yes, these people were people living about 200 or so metres away from me house. They left their houses and came and found shelter in my village -- in my house. They were from the same village but from a higher up place, and they were about 40 persons. My family -- extended family members were 17 persons. So they were from the same village but living a little bit further away. Is the answer I gave you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Two hundred metres away from your house? Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Two hundred, 300, far from the Peja town. Called Fushe e Pejes, Peja Field. I don't know how more explicitly can I describe it. It is part of the village but it is called Fushe e Pejes, Peja Field.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many men were there, say between the ages of 20 and 60 save for yourself? Were your brothers there as well, as well as the neighbours who had arrived? Out of the total figure, how many men were there aged between 20 and 60?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: When do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: At that time.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: You mean the people who were gathered in the courtyard of my house?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Let me try to be more precise. You say that at the moment when you left the house, when your mother asked you to go out so as not to be killed, you say that those 40 guests remained in the house in addition to your family and you left. That is, I presume, the 14th of May, 1999. I'm asking you this: Who remain in the house? your brothers? your neighbours? Were there any men there, or was it all just women and children in the house?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: In my statement I said women and children. You have the statement. If you ask me, I can -- if their Honour, Judges, ask me questions I may answer them, but otherwise you have everything in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: In the statement you said: "I went a distance away so as not to be killed in front of my family. The rest of the family and some 40 guests who were in my house remained behind." You did not mention any women and children. That is why I'm asking you this. Were there any men in your house when you left? Where were your brothers, for instance, since you said you had two? In your statement, in paragraph 7 in the statement of 2008, and paragraph 3 of your statement from 1999, this is what you say, and my conclusion is that everyone remained in the house except for yourself. That's why I'm asking you were there any men there. If you can tell me, please.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I am repeating that after I saw the police and the army, I went home. I told everyone what I saw. We were having coffee. The people went in the direction of the village. I remained at home. I went to my first neighbour, told them what was happening, and I saw them leave the house and head somewhere. I don't know where. This is the truth. And I was not asked then at the time when I gave the statement where and who.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: That is why I'm asking you for the last time. Did your two brothers remain in the house as well as some other men or not on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: As I said, they left before me. I left afterwards. As soon as I told them that the army and the police had entered the village, they left. I remained in the house. When my mother insisted that I leave too, I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Berisha, since in 1999, as well as in 2008, you used the term "paramilitary" on several occasions. What do you understand by that term?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: In your interview to the investigators of this Tribunal, on several occasions you used the word "paramilitary." I'm interested in the following: What do you understand that term to mean, and then I will have a follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't know. You can ask me a follow-up question or a next question, and if I remember, then I can come back to this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, I can conclude that you do not know what "paramilitary" means.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I'm not saying that I don't know, but I will not respond to this question. I'm talking about police and army. I don't know what you call them, paramilitaries or something else. I don't know what others call them. They might as well call them paramilitaries, but for me, for a person who saw everything with his own eyes, they were police and military. This would be my answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I agree with you as regards 2008 but not 1999, because in 1999 you mentioned paramilitaries, and I think in 2008 you did too. In any case, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, as I understand the evidence of the witness, it is that he did not use the word "paramilitary." He can't say what whoever it was that interviewed him may have written down, but he says he did not use the word "paramilitary." Now, that may explain why your question is not relevant in his mind to what events happened in April and in May, because he says, "I only spoke of the police and the military." I've understood you correctly there, have I, Mr. Berisha? The witness acknowledges yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would have understood the witness had he not -- I understand, Your Honour. I would have understood him, but he had said that he did not wish to respond. If he had remained with the answer, "I don't know," I would have understood that. In any case, I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: How many kilometres away from Cuska one comes across the village of Pavlan?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: They are adjacent to each other if I understood you correctly. There is no kilometre between them. There's just like a line, a borderline that divides the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: What about the village of Zahac?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Possibly two and a half or three kilometres far from Qyshk. From Qyshk.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: The village of Lodja?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: From Qyshk?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Lodja.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: From Qyshk you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Three or more kilometres. I don't know for sure. I'm talking about distance as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge whether anyone from your village of Cuska belonged to the KLA?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I know that Agim Ceku was the commander of the KLA. For others, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: In addition to Agim Ceku, do you know of anyone else from the village being a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't know of anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Given that Lodja is only three kilometres away from Cuska, were you a witness to or do you have any knowledge of the fierce fighting between the KLA and the Serb forces, that is to say the military, in 1998?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I didn't see it myself, but I did hear gunshots.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of any fighting that took place?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: There were fightings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps from your neighbours?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: [No interpretation] --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What are your brother's names?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: -- reputation. Can you repeat your question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: What are the names of your brothers with whom you shared the household?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Nezir Berisha and Fadil Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Were you ever accused by the security forces of Serbia that you or your brother Nezir took part in the illegal smuggling of arms via Decani, Glodjani, and Cuska, as well as into the field, onwards?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear about this. I was never accused in my whole life for such incidents. I wish it were true, this what you just put to me, but as I said, this was the first time I heard about such accusations, from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there anyone else in Cuska who shared the same first and last name?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: There is by my first name but not by my last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: The same first and last name, Berisha, Hazir.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: By name Hazir, yes. By last name, Berisha, Hazir Berisha, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who is Tahir Kelmendi? From Cuska.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: He lives in my village, co-villager of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: How far is his house from yours?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: About 300 metres as the crow flies. He lives in another road, and I live in another road in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see him during that time, around the 14th of May?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: No. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of certain events in the area and municipality of Pec pertaining to any Serb civilians being kidnapped? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about whether -- or, rather, that there were many killed members of the police and military in the area of Pec?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't know why you're asking me this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of that or not? That's all I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know of Salipur, a policeman from Pec being killed by KLA terrorists? Do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I would say the opposite of what you're saying. Salipur was killed. I don't know when and by whom. I don't know who are these terrorists that you're saying. I am here as a witness, and it's the other side that committed terror and terrorism there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My question was this: Do you know of any killed soldiers or policemen? You said you didn't know of any terrorists but, however, I conclude that you did know of Salipur being killed, although you don't know who killed him. In any case, I'll move on. Before the events in 1999 and until May of that year, did you see any patrols, army or police patrols, comprising any members of Serb ethnicity from the nearby settlements of Pec, Nakle, Gorazdice in uniform? Did you see such people passing through your village or did you have occasion to see them in Pec when you went there?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: You mean soldiers or policemen wearing uniforms? Can you please put to me shorter and clearer questions, because I really don't understand your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I mean all of them, soldiers, policemen, those in camouflage uniforms, those with bandanas, with hats. Did you see any neighbours of yours in any uniforms or outfits of that sort?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: If you're referring to Serbs, that's a different thing. If you're referring to neighbours living around my house, then that's a different thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: My question was clear. Nakle, Gorazdice, and Pec. I limited myself to your neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: In Nakle, Gorazdice, wherever you're saying, the Serbs had uniforms issued to them by the state. They -- all of them had uniforms in their homes. Everybody was aware of that, and I don't know why you're asking me this question. It was public knowledge that they had uniforms issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Was any of them present on the 14th of May, 1999, in your village when the massacre took place?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I did mention those that I saw. Maybe there were others from Gorazdice.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the name of the person.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whereas the others, I don't know where they came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: The people you referred to are indeed Popovic and Kastratovic. You say you recognised them since you knew them by sight. Where did you see them before that? And you saw some of the photographs. What can you tell me about Kastratovic, for instance? Where does he hail from? What was his age? Do you know what his occupation was, and where did you personally see them -- see him, because you said you knew him by sight.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: As I said, I knew him by sight. I saw him when he came to Qyshk on the 14th of May and on the 16th and the 17th. This would be my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Had you ever seen him before that point in time? Kastratovic, I mean.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Are you saying before the 14th? I think I was clear. On the 14th and also on the 16th or the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: May or April?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: We have two separate dates, 16th and 17th of April and 14th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Was Kastratovic wearing the same uniform on both occasions you saw him, Mr. Berisha?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: What sort of uniform was it? What did it look like?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I think I mentioned it several times earlier. It was a green camouflage uniforms -- uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: What sort of weapons did he sport?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: When did you first see his photograph?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: After the NATO troops entered. We're talking about his photograph; right? After the NATO troops entered Kosova, they found photographs in their homes and on various locations where they photographed themselves. They brought them to me and asked me if I knew those persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did they bring the photographs to you, or did they show you Kastratovic's photograph on the screen of a laptop?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I already said the following: They had left photographs behind in their homes, and then they brought these photographs to us because they didn't have computer with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Who brought you the photographs? Who are they?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't remember who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you know Salipur by sight, the one you said conducted himself toward the ethnic Albanians in a particularly sadistic way, the policeman from Pec? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: He was tall and thin and referred to by his nickname Salipur. I didn't know him in person, but I saw him in Peja on several occasions. Therefore, I knew that he was policeman even before the critical time. And I saw with my own eyes how he maltreated occasional passers-by.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: When did you see his photograph? Was it on the same day you saw Kastratovic's photograph?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who was it who showed you his photograph?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I already told you several times I don't remember who.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see Popovic before the 14th of May and the 17th of April, and if so, where?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I didn't see him before these dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did you observe anything peculiar about Popovic, either in his gait, in the way he walks, or in the way he talks?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: When was his photograph shown to you and in what form? Was it a photograph or was it a laptop image?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I will repeat it as many times as you wish. After the NATO troops entered Kosovo, these photographs were found and they were shown to me. I don't know by whom. To be more clear, I don't remember who brought those photographs to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: To avoid putting the same question to you about other individuals, is what you say the same for all the photographs that were shown to you?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: For these photographs on which I identified the participants in the events, all of them were brought to me after NATO troops entered Kosova. Who brought them to me, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Nebojsa Minic, did you know him before the 14th of May events?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: 14th of May. I referred to the incident before the 14th of May, that is, 16th and 17th of April, and if you keep asking me the same question, I'll keep answering you in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: My question is as following: Did you know Nebojsa Minic before the events of the 16th and 17th of April and the 14th of May? Did you ever see him before that period?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You say that you were brought these photographs following the KFOR arrival in Kosovo. What did they do with the photographs afterwards? Did they leave them behind in your hands or did they take them along?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: No. They just showed me the photographs. They didn't leave any of the photographs with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Since we are supposed to have your technical break an hour and a half into our session, I will now put one more question to you before the break. In your testimony today, you did not mention anyone bringing any photographs to you. Rather, you said that a book was given to you by way of a gift for your participation in the investigation and that it was through the book that you came to recognise these individuals. Now you stated something quite different. Can you please account for or reconcile for us these two statements that you made in the space of half an hour that all of us were able to hear in the courtroom today?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: The truth is that immediately after the war these pictures were brought to us, but even later the book that you mentioned contained these photographs, and I identified the same persons. The same persons brought the book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient break, then, Mr. Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before the break can I tender the questionnaire that I referred to as D003-0348 into evidence lest I should forget after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned D00117, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, we're going to have another break now, and we'll continue until about 7.00. Is that convenient? Very well. We will -- sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Sorry -- thank you. We will adjourn now, then, until 10 past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will resume my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: In order to fully clear up the relevant portion of your statement, I will have to continue putting questions to you about the individuals you purportedly recognised in the photographs. In paragraph 69 of the 2008 statement, you say: "I did not recognise anybody I knew." Am I right if I say that you had not known any of these individuals earlier on, but you subsequently recognised them in the photographs you were shown as those who participated in the events of the 14th of May or the 17th of April? Is that what this particular sentence from your statement means?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Your question is rather long. Can you please make it shorter so that I can follow it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 69, you state: " ... but did not recognise anybody I knew," and you were referring to soldiers and policemen, and you say that you could not know -- "I'm unable to say what units any ever of them operated with but I did not recognise anybody I knew." Therefore, my question: Can I conclude that you didn't know any of these persons before the events of the 14th of May, 1999? And in respect of some of them, you said that you also saw them on the 17th of April. Am I right in drawing this conclusion or not?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: If you want me to please you, I said before the 16th or the 17th I didn't know them, the ones that I identified by names, that I saw in several photos. But if you're asking me about something else, then I might give you another explanation. This is my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That was precisely my question, the one that you answered. I'd like to know the following: This is a question put to you by my learned friend which did not receive a clear answer. You say that you believe that whatever happened happened because the Serbs took revenge. You say that revenge was the cause of all these actions on their part. Can you tell me what exactly you meant by saying that revenge was at the root of all of their actions?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I think I was clear enough when I said in answer to the question that it was revenge against NATO, because allegedly it was us who asked for NATO, and that being the case, they took revenge against us, killing Albanians and doing what I have testified about here, to cut a long story short.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I conclude that prior to that there had never been any hostilities between the two nations?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that, because it's common knowledge both for Albanians and for the Serbs that the hostilities started much earlier on, but I'm speaking about the revenge they engaged in after the NATO interfered, because in that case they wanted to do more than they had already done. They started to purge the villages from Albanians, to send them to Albania, maltreating people and doing many other bad things, whereas in our case we were unfortunate enough to be killed, but the actual hostilities had started much earlier. I might add something. May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't have any hostilities with the Serb families living with us, but these hostilities involved the Serbian authorities. I didn't have anything against my neighbours, Serb neighbours. We didn't kill anyone. We didn't set fire to anyone's house, but what you are putting to me refers to the authorities, to the government, not to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. You said that there were three Serb families living in your village, i.e., the village of Cuska. You said that there had never been any hostility in their respect. Did they continue living in your village?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: They lived there until they themselves decided to leave. They remained in Qyshk until KFOR left the place, but then they left for Serbia. I have no other answer to give you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At paragraphs 43 and 47, you say that you observed the commander making a gesture which made you believe that he had ordered certain ethnic Albanians from Cuska to be executed by those under his command. You described his gesture as him placing his hands one above the other and moving them and that you understood this to believe an order for execution. And at paragraph 47 when you say you observed a soldier making the same gesture to his commander, that you believed that this meant that the order had been carried out. Can you tell me, what made you conclude, first of all, that this was an order for an execution; and secondly, that the second gesture, the same gesture, meant that the order had been executed? Where did you get that from?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I came to that conclusion after hearing the gunshots and after seeing the smoke coming out of the houses. By that gesture, that was my personal inference, I understand that that was the case, and in fact it came out to be true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did you subsequently recognise the commander who made this gesture or the soldier who reported with the same gesture that the order had been carried out in the photographs you were shown?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Which soldier are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Apparently in paragraph 47 you say that the soldier made the same gesture to his commander. He crossed his hands in the same way, and you say that you took this to mean that the man had been -- that the order had been carried out; whereas in paragraph 43, you mention this gesture for the first time, and you say that you understood this to mean that the men should be killed; whereas at paragraph 47 you said: "Upon seeing the same gesture again, I took this to mean that the men had been killed." The second time, it was one of the men making the gesture, not the commander.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. The soldiers who made that gesture with his hands is Popovic. That was the one I recognised, and I think I mentioned that in my statement. There were over 70 persons present there. I couldn't recognise them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- commander?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I'm repeating. Since he was the person who gave orders -- he was one of the two who gave orders. I thought that he was their leader and their commander. And I'm repeating. That was my assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did you recognise the commander, the one who was referred to in paragraph 43 of your statement and who issued the order by making the gesture the way you understood it?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I meant Srecko Popovic. He was the person whom I recognised in the middle of April and on -- he was again there on the 14th. But I think I've answered this question for the umpteenth time. I have no other answer to give you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Throughout this time, although your family was told that it would be driven out of Kosovo, the families did, nevertheless, remain in the area, although moving locally.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the name of the locality mentioned by Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The town of Pec.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please repeat your question? I am not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did your entire family remain in Kosovo throughout the time?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone specifically from Cuska -- was anyone from Cuska driven out to Albania or Montenegro, regardless? At any rate, across the borders of Kosovo. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I said in my statement they took them until the entrance to the city two times, and then they returned them. The reason why they asked them to return and why didn't let them leave, I don't know. I only know that the police and the army sent them back when they arrived at the entrance to the city. The order was given to them to go back to the village. And this is my answer, and I have repeated it several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, I am right in saying that nobody from the village of Cuska was driven out across the border of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I'm talking about that day. I don't know about other times. That date, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have information about any other period of time in 1999, specifically about Cuska?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't recall anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My next question: You said that the room you were in which was set on fire, you left that room by clambering out through the window. In addition to the injuries suffered to your legs and in addition to the fact that you could hardly breathe for the smoke that was around, were you at all enveloped by the flames? Were you engulfed by the flames?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I'm repeating that because of the smoke, because of that gas that was thrown in the room, my face caught fire. And because of the burning and the gas that I inhaled, I couldn't breathe and that I left that room. I think I gave a very clear answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you were wounded to your left leg and that it was an entry/exit wound. You also said that there was a shot which broke the shank of your right leg and that your right knee was also injured. You said that you treated your wounds for about a month, and then on the 15th or the 16th of June you went to the hospital in Pec. Therefore, a month later. You told us who it was who took you in and dressed your wound. You said that you gave all the medical documentation concerning your injuries to the investigators. Or you told them that they could go and see the documentation for themselves in the hospital. This isn't clear. Did you really provide them with medical documentation from the Pec hospital or did you merely give them your approval, your consent for them to go to the hospital and look at your medical file there?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't understand. What are you asking me about? Whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to paragraph 74 of your statement from May 2008.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I gave what I was asked for. I don't know anything about the Peja hospital. Can you make the question clearer? I don't understand it. Make it shorter, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 74 of your statement: "As a result of the incident, I have scarring to my legs," et cetera, et cetera. "I give the ICTY my permission to examine any medical records in relation to my treatment for these injuries." My question is: What medical records are you referring to and from what hospital? Is it the Pec hospital?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I showed them the wounds, and I told them that if it was necessary for them to trace this issue further, they were free to do so. I have mentioned the date when I went to the Peja hospital. It was about six weeks later, I think. You have my wound as a document to show everything. You don't need anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Am I correct in saying that on the 14th or the 15th of June you went to the Pec hospital to continue your treatment in 1999?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. Either the 14th or the 15th of June it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How long did you remain in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't remember how long I remained. I think about three weeks, but the recovery period lasted more than a year, because I had to undergo surgery in my right leg which was broken, and it took me more than a year to recover, but I had to undergo surgery in the Italian -- KFOR Italian hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Were you operated on in the hospital in Pec?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: They put the plaster, then after a year I underwent surgery. The reason for that was they didn't have the necessary means and equipment, and they hoped that my leg would recover, and after a year or so I was obliged to go to the Italian hospital, KFOR Italian hospital. They admitted me in and operated on me there. You can inquire there if you want to prove what I'm telling you is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: What was the name of the doctor who treated you in the hospital in Pec?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Who administered me the first aid, who put the plaster on my -- on my right leg was Isak, Isak Alicani [phoen], orthopaedician.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Concerning this incident you went through, were you subsequently given any documentation from the Pec hospital or the Italian hospital, any discharge forms or case histories that you handed over to the investigators of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I didn't get anything from the Peja hospital, but I did get a couple of such medical records from the Italian one, and I think they are with the investigators. One of them is Samuel.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the proper name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your answers. My last question concerning your medical status is this: Do you believe them to have it or are you certain you handed those records over, the medical records and reports?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Only from the Italian KFOR medical staff. They might have gotten a copy of the records. I've attended many check-ups, daily, weekly, monthly check-ups. I think there was no need for me to go into detail with them for each and every record, because my injuries were proof to what had happened to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: The last set of questions I have for you in my cross has to do with the members of the Jasovic family. You mentioned certain family members by their first and last names as people that you saw carrying a Serbian flag. Could you please clarify the context of that part of your story for me since it was unclear to me after I read the statement. These were your neighbours.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't say whether they had uniforms or not. What I said was that they came to the village. They were carrying smaller flags. They came exactly on the spot where we were gathered. I saw one of them with a lady. I don't know who this lady was. Later on, two others came also carrying flags and went exactly on the spot where the incident occurred near the graveyard. From there they continued along another path, and from thereon I could no longer see them. I don't know where they went to. This is what I saw with my own eyes, and I'm stating it with full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: I believe I understand now, but the entire background about the sporting of flags is unclear to me. Did they have uniforms on, and what in general was taking place concerning the Jasovic family members referred to in this context?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: What context are you talking about? I really don't get your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: You said you saw Velibor Jasovic, I believe, as well as some other people of the Jasovic family carrying a Serbian flag. You knew those people since you were neighbours. What was that situation in particular that you saw them? Did they have weapons on that occasion? Did they wear uniforms? That is what I would like to know.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: As I said, Vidoje and another lady and the others, they came carrying the smaller flags. I didn't mention any uniforms. Where I saw him, he was there in a company of a lady whom I didn't know, carrying a flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Without a uniform? He did not wear a uniform?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: When I -- when I saw them, no, they -- he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this concludes my cross-examination of this witness, and thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djordjevic. Ms. Gopalan, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Berisha, I have a few questions for you arising from Mr. Djordjevic's cross-examination. You were asked today about uniforms that had been issued to Serbs. At page 56, line 6, you said: "Serbs had uniforms issued to them by the state. They all had uniforms in their homes." Could you tell us, Mr. Berisha, when was it these uniforms were issued to the Serbs, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't recall the exact date, but I would say it was in the beginning of 1998, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you say these uniforms were issued by the state, are you able to explain what exactly or who you are referring to when you say "the state"?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. When I say the state, what I mean is that the police and the army are part of the state. They're commanded by the state. In early 1998, if I'm not mistaken, it was the police that began to distribute uniforms to those locations inhabited by Serbs, whereas the areas inhabited by Albanians were not issued with uniforms, Qyshk village being one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: If you know, Mr. Berisha, in addition to the uniforms being distributed to these locations inhabited by Serbs, do you know if anything else was issued together with the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Together with uniforms, weapons were issued. I wasn't there to see the distribution, but all of them were armed. There are facts that corroborate this statement of mine. They were issued both uniforms and weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And in relation to the uniforms being issued, how did you know that these uniforms were issued?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: From the media and the citizens, and on several locations during the war I saw them wearing uniforms. If you do a more thorough investigation into this, you will come to the same facts to what I'm telling you now.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Berisha. You were asked some questions today about an individual named Salipur, and at page 58, line 12, you refer to having seen Salipur maltreating occasional passers-by. Could you tell us when you saw Salipur maltreat these passers-by, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: This occurred before 1998, if I'm not mistaken. It happened before 1998 in the town of Peja.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you say "maltreating," what exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: What I mean is that he would stop them, ask for their documents, and on many occasions he would beat the citizens in the presence of others. This once happened in the market, in the grocery market, in Peja town, and I personally witnessed this incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. If you recall, how many of these incidents did you witness yourself?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't recall. With the exception of this one that I mentioned, I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Berisha. You were also asked some questions today about the hand gesture made by the senior soldier which you took to be an order for execution. This is at page 64, line 4. And you replied saying you came to that conclusion after hearing gunshots and after having seen smoke coming out of the house. Could you tell us which house you were referring to in this case? This is in response to a question in relation to paragraph 47 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: I'm referring to the house of Syl Gashi from which Isa Gashi survived.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: How many men were taken to the house of Syl Gashi? If you know.

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: Approximately 12 or 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And with the exception of Isa Gashi who you have mentioned, what happened to the remaining men who were taken to Syl Gashi's house?

utterances.speaker: HAZIR ISUF BERISHA
utterances.text: They were all killed and burnt.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Berisha. I have no further questions for you today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Gopalan. Mr. Berisha, you'll be pleased to know that completes the questions for you. The Chamber would like to thank you for coming to The Hague and for the assistance you have been able to give, and we have now not only your statement but also the answers you've been able to give today to assist us in our consideration of this case. We thank you very much, and you may now, of course, return to your ordinary --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, Your Honours, I would also like to extend my gratitude to you and the Prosecutors, as well as the lawyer for his provoking answers. I'm here to tell the truth and nothing but the truth. I am a person who went through the incident that we discussed today. I am stating here with full responsibility that all these things I experienced myself, and I really regret the fact that for all these years they didn't find the time to express their regret for what happened in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The court officer will now show you from the court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There seems little point in commencing the next witness at this hour, so we will adjourn until the morning. Could I mention we will be following an unusual timetable in the morning, because we need to adjourn at 10 minutes to 10.00, as the new registrar will be sworn in and the Judges will be present on that occasion. We expect -- but we cannot be entirely confident, but we expect to be able to return to court by 10.30. So we will adjourn at 10 minutes before 10.00, and we hope to be back by 10.30 to continue the hearing with two further sessions. We should not lose very many minutes, but we will have a different timetable for the morning. With those words, we will now adjourn to resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
